title: Battle of Yarmouk
summary: In August 636 a Rashidun Muslim army under Khalid ibn al-Walid defeated a Byzantine army near the Yarmouk River in southern Syria. Sources describe a decisive Muslim victory on the final day, and EBSCO says Syria, Palestine and Egypt were in Muslim hands by 645.

uncertainty.note: Sources agree on the dates; they differ on the length (four days vs six days).

where.modern_name: Yarmouk River, Jordan/Syria border region (PROXY pin; battlefield not located by the sources)
where.historical_name: Near the Yarmuk River, Byzantine Syria

importance.justification: EBSCO links the Byzantine defeat to the loss of Syria, Palestine and Egypt within a few years.

audience_note: Concerns a battle with heavy casualties.

sources.title: OpenStreetMap Nominatim result for Yarmouk River

reviewer_note: PROXY PIN at a point on the Yarmouk River (OSM); sources say only "near the Yarmuk River" / a plain north of Wadi Yarmuk. EBSCO says the battle "unfolded over four days" while its header and WHE give 15-20 August. WHE does not state outnumbering for the Byzantines; it says the Rashidun army was heavily outnumbered.
